tho: The morning mist still veils the pier,
The ferry waits, the way is clear;
Hold steady, friend, and pull as one,
The eastern bank is nearly won.
loiGiai: Morning mist still hangs over the landing, yet the ferry is ready to cross. This verse encourages you to begin what you have long been planning. The far bank isn't as distant as it seems; keep one steady heart and pull the oar in an even rhythm. Don't wait for every bit of mist to clear, because the way grows plain once you are already on it.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: At home, a kind word in the morning can set a warm tone for the whole day. Start the conversation yourself instead of waiting for others to speak first.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: New work is waiting to be started. Make a simple plan, finish the first piece this week, and adjust as you learn.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Rise a little earlier, take a gentle walk or breathe deeply in the fresh air; your body will wake up and your spirits will lift.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: This is a good time to begin a new subject or skill. Set small goals and study a little every day; you will be surprised how far you get.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If someone has caught your heart, be sincere and unhurried. No need to rush, but don't stay on this side of the river only watching.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money comes from steady, honest effort. Start writing down your spending and set aside a small amount from today.

loiKhuyen: Take the first step today, however small. Row evenly, keep your heart steady, and the far bank will draw near.

tho: A little stream meets stone and stays,
Not angry, it just finds new ways;
Soft water still runs clear and bright,
And slowly grows a river's might.
loiGiai: A small stream meets a rock in its path. It doesn't rage or stop; it gently finds a way around. Because of this its water stays clear and in time it becomes a great river. This verse reminds you that gentleness isn't weakness. When obstacles appear, stay calm, look for another way, keep your heart clear, and move slowly but steadily.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When things aren't smooth at home, speak softly rather than trying to win. Words as gentle as water can smooth sharp edges.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: When work gets stuck, don't keep pushing straight into the blockage. Ask a colleague or try a different approach; the way out is often right beside you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body needs a steady rhythm like a flowing stream. Drink enough water, sleep on time and move within your strength. If tiredness lasts, see a doctor for peace of mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If a hard lesson doesn't make sense yet, don't lose heart. Go back to the basics and ask teachers or friends; knowledge soaks in like water into soil.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love needs gentleness and patience. Don't force the other person to follow your way; listen more and you will understand each other better.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income may not rise quickly, but steady saving turns a small stream into a river. Stay away from offers to get rich fast.

loiKhuyen: When you meet a stone, flow around it rather than crash into it. Keep your heart clear, move slowly and steadily, and you will arrive.

tieuDe: Boat Home to a Quiet Pier
tho: At dusk the little boat comes in
Where lamplight glows to welcome kin;
Around the table, young and old,
The family gathers, safe from cold.
loiGiai: As evening falls, a small boat ties up at the familiar pier, where a lamp hangs by the front door. This verse carries a feeling of calm and settling. It reminds you to cherish your home and the people waiting for you. After busy days out in the world, make time to come back, share a meal together and listen to the stories of your elders.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This is a good time for reunion. Call relatives who live far away, or plan a meal this week with the whole family around the table.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work is fairly stable for now. Finish your tasks during working hours and avoid bringing work home, so time with family stays protected.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A full home meal, eaten slowly with cheerful talk, is good for body and mind. Older family members should have regular health check-ups.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: After studying, allow yourself to rest with your family. Sometimes a relative's advice is exactly what clears up what you are unsure about.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: The people who truly care for you are the ones who hope you come home safely. Treasure those who quietly leave a light on for you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Talk household spending over together. A shared family savings fund helps everyone feel more secure.

loiKhuyen: Come home a little earlier today, share a meal with your loved ones and say one word of thanks.

tho: A bamboo bridge sways in the breeze;
Walk slow and steady, cross with ease.
Though gusts may make your footing sway,
Hold fast the rail, and keep your way.
loiGiai: The bamboo bridge across the canal may sway, yet it carries people safely to the other side if they walk calmly and keep a firm grip on the handrail. This verse is a gentle call for care: don't let a gust of wind make you panic and let go. While you aren't yet steady, lean on the basics, on trustworthy people and on small, sure steps.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When things feel unsteady at home, keep the familiar routines together, like shared meals and greetings. These are the family's handrail.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If you are in a new job or an unfamiliar role, go step by step, learn the process carefully and don't take shortcuts just to save time.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Be careful when traveling, especially on wet, slippery days. If your body shows unusual signs, see a doctor early rather than ignoring them.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: An exam or a hard assignment ahead may worry you. Review the foundations, secure the parts you know first, then work on the hard ones.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: When a relationship wobbles a little, don't rush into angry words. Hold on to respect like a handrail and things will settle.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: This isn't the time to take risks with money. Keep an emergency fund, spend only on what is needed and think twice about big decisions.

loiKhuyen: Walk calmly and keep a firm grip. A little slower and safe is better than hurried and shaken.

tho: The lake lies still as polished glass,
Its face reflects the clouds that pass;
Let your own heart grow calm and slow,
Rest well, and peace will start to grow.
loiGiai: When the wind dies down, the lake is as smooth as a mirror and reflects every cloud. The heart is the same: only when it is less stirred can we see clearly what we truly need. This verse advises you to set aside quiet time and rest at the right moment. You don't always have to do more; sometimes sitting still is the best way to keep going.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Create a quiet corner at home, with less noise and fewer screens in the evening, so everyone can rest and talk gently.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't make decisions while upset. Let things settle overnight; in the morning you will see the way forward more clearly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body needs rest. Get enough sleep and try a few minutes of slow breathing each day. If sleeplessness continues, ask a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study in a quiet space and silence your phone notifications. When the mind settles, new knowledge sinks in like clouds reflected on a lake.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Calm your heart to understand your own feelings before asking someone else to understand you. Serenity makes love last.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money calls for a calm mind right now. Avoid impulse buying; write down what you want and check a few days later whether you still need it.

loiKhuyen: Each day, spend ten minutes sitting still and breathing slowly. Once the heart is calm, everything looks clearer.

tho: Drop after drop, year after year,
Wears hardest stone, so persevere;
Keep faith in learning, firm and true,
A little daily carries you.
loiGiai: Small drops of water falling steadily through the years can wear down even a hard stone. This verse encourages perseverance: you don't need great strength, only daily steadiness. Learning, work and good habits all take shape from small efforts repeated. Keep your resolve firm, and in time everything will come out well.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Good things at home grow from small daily acts: a caring question, a hand with the chores. Keep doing them without waiting for a big occasion.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Long projects need steadiness. Break the work into small parts, finish one every day and don't leave it all to the last minute.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A good habit such as walking, stretching or sleeping early, kept steadily, brings longer-lasting health than any rushed effort.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying a little every day beats cramming in one night. Set a fixed review schedule and take notes; knowledge will sink in deeply.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts through steady care, not grand promises. Notice the small things the other person needs.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Save a small amount every month and over time it becomes real savings. Stay away from gambling and promises of unusually high returns.

loiKhuyen: Choose one good habit and keep it every day for thirty days. Small but steady becomes great in time.

tho: The mountain road winds through the cloud;
Walk steady, slow, with head unbowed.
The mist will lift, the sky will glow;
The summit waits for those who go.
loiGiai: The winding mountain pass is hidden in cloud and travelers cannot yet see the top. This verse asks for patience: keep going evenly and slowly, and don't rush at the cost of safety. The clouds will lift and the sky will brighten. Those who keep a steady heart will find the summit waiting, and the road behind them will become something to treasure.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When the family is going through a hard stretch, walk it together step by step. Talk things through and share chores so no one carries the load alone.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Results at work may not show right away. Keep a steady pace and note your progress each week so you can see yourself moving forward.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't push your body beyond its limits. Rest between efforts and eat well. If something feels wrong, see a doctor instead of enduring it.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Some subjects are like a mountain pass, harder the higher you climb. Ask those who went before you for directions and keep practicing each type of problem.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If you aren't yet sure of someone's heart, don't jump to conclusions. Time and sincerity will clear the mist.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income may be slow, but keep honest work and careful spending. Avoid borrowing to chase things you don't yet need.

loiKhuyen: Keep an even pace and don't hurry. The clouds are only for now; a steady heart reaches the top.

tho: Last night the sea rose wild and high;
This morning, sun climbs up the sky.
Our joys and sorrows rise like foam;
Stop clinging, and peace finds its home.
loiGiai: Last night the sea was rough; this morning the waves are still and the sun is high. The joys and sorrows of life are like waves too, stirring for a while and then calming again. This verse advises you to set down the anger and worry that have passed. Not to forget everything, but to stop clinging, so your heart grows lighter and can welcome a peaceful new day.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If something unpleasant just happened at home, be the first to make peace. A shared meal or an apology can calm the sea again.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Something at work didn't go as hoped, but it is over. Take the lesson, note what to fix, and focus on the task in front of you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Long-lasting worry wears the body down. Practice slow breathing, take walks and talk with someone you trust. If sadness lasts many days, consider seeing a professional.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: One poor exam doesn't define you. Look over the mistakes, rest a little, then return to studying with a fresh mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Hurt feelings in love come and go like waves. Don't hold on to harsh words; talk openly once you are both calm.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: If you have lost some money, don't try to win it back by taking risks. Stay calm and start saving again; that is the sure path.

loiKhuyen: Write down what weighs on your heart, read it once, then put it away. Letting go lightens the heart.

tieuDe: The Far Peak in the Clouds
tho: The distant peak is lost in white,
The misty trail is out of sight;
Yet good things wait, as mountains stay,
When fog lifts, green will light the day.
loiGiai: The distant mountain is still hidden in clouds, the path up unclear and the old trail wrapped in mist. This verse speaks of calm waiting. Good things are still there, just as the mountain still stands; the time for them to appear hasn't yet come. When the mist lifts, you will see the mountain in full green. While you wait, take good care of yourself.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Some family hopes cannot come true right away. Be patient, add your small part each day and don't blame each other for the slowness.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Opportunities may not be clearly visible yet. Use this time to build your skills, so you are ready when the moment comes.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Recovery takes time. Follow your doctor's guidance, rest well and don't be impatient to feel better overnight.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Results that don't show immediately don't mean your effort was wasted. Keep studying; your understanding is quietly growing.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Good love is never in a hurry. The right person may not have arrived yet, or may already be near without you noticing. Live well and keep your heart open.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't grow impatient and chase quick ways to make money. Keep steady work and save regularly; when the mist lifts, the path will be clear.

loiKhuyen: Not seeing the mountain doesn't mean it isn't there. Take care of yourself while the mist clears.

tho: The river splits two ways ahead;
Each branch to gentle land is led.
Once you have weighed it, walk with grace,
And don't look back at every pace.
loiGiai: The river divides into two branches, and both flow toward good land. This verse comes when you stand before a choice. Think it over, listen to your heart and ask someone you trust; but once you have decided, step forward boldly and don't keep looking back until doubt holds you in place. Any path walked with sincerity has something worth learning.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If the family must make a big decision, let everyone share their view. Once decided, support it together without blaming later.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Facing two directions at work, write down the gains and losses of each and choose the one that fits your values.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Long indecision can bring stress and poor sleep. Set yourself a deadline to decide, then let your mind rest.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: When choosing a major, a school or a subject, rely on what you love and what you are truly able to do. Once chosen, study wholeheartedly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If your heart is torn between two ways, be honest with yourself and with others. Clarity is the kindest path.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: For money choices, prefer the safe and transparent option. Don't choose only because of promises of high profit.

loiKhuyen: Think carefully, then decide. Once you have chosen, walk with your whole heart and don't let doubt hold you back.

tho: Two people share a single boat,
In rhythm, calmly they will float;
If one should slip and miss a beat,
The other waits, and so they meet.
loiGiai: Two people paddle one boat, and only when they keep the same rhythm does it glide smoothly. Sometimes one misses a stroke and the other slows down to wait, and then together they reach the shore. This verse is about unity, tolerance and give-and-take. In family, love or work, patience with one another is the oar that carries the boat far.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Everyone at home has their own temperament. When someone is tired or makes a mistake, slow down and lend a hand rather than blame.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Teamwork needs clear roles and a shared pace. If a colleague falls behind, ask what support they need.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Invite a family member to exercise or walk with you in the afternoon. With a companion, good habits last longer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study groups work when everyone contributes. Be patient explaining to a friend who hasn't understood; you will understand it better too.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when two people know how to wait for each other. Don't count who does more; look in the same direction together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Shared money matters should be transparent and discussed in advance. Planning spending together avoids misunderstandings.

loiKhuyen: When the person beside you misses a beat, slow down and wait. Only in rhythm does the boat reach the shore.

tho: The tide comes in, the sea is wide;
The boat with nets prepared can ride.
Like tides, our chances ebb and flow;
Mend nets and sails; when it's time, go.
loiGiai: The tide rises and the estuary opens wide. Any boat with its nets ready can ride the current out to sea. This verse is encouraging: an opportunity may be on its way, but only those who are prepared can fully receive it. Check your gear, your skills and your plans, so when the time comes you can set out steadily and return safely.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The family may have good news or an important occasion ahead. Prepare carefully together and share tasks clearly so everyone feels at ease.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Opportunities at work are opening. Update your résumé, sharpen your skills and take on new tasks with confidence when they are offered.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: To meet opportunity, your health must be ready. Eat regularly, sleep enough and don't stay up late night after night for work.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: An exam or competition is coming. Review with a plan and prepare your documents early so the day holds no surprises.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If you meet someone you connect with, be natural and sincere. An open heart is the best way to welcome love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: There may be extra income from honest work. Read terms carefully and avoid vague investment offers.

loiKhuyen: Check your gear today. The right time comes to those who are ready.

tieuDe: The Stepping Stone in the Stream
tho: Beside the stream a stone was laid
So feet stay dry where travelers wade;
Remember those who helped you through,
Who set the stone, though no one knew.
loiGiai: By the stream lies a stone someone placed there, so that people crossing can head home with dry feet. The one who set the stone asked for no recognition. This verse is about gratitude: what we have today has often been quietly built by many hands. Remember them, and know that you too can be the one who quietly sets a stone for those who come after.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Say thank you to your parents, grandparents and all who have cared for you. A simple thank-you warms the whole home.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Today's success includes the effort of colleagues and those who came before. Recognize them, and be willing to guide newcomers.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Thank your body for working hard every day by caring for it: eat well, rest enough and have regular check-ups.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Teachers and friends have helped you learn. Show your gratitude and share notes and experience so you all improve together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Treasure the small things the other person has done for you. Noticing and saying thanks deepens love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Knowing what is enough and being grateful for what you have helps you spend wisely. Give some time to help someone in need with practical deeds.

loiKhuyen: Today, thank someone who once helped you, and do one small good deed that no one needs to know about.

tho: The old stone bridge is green with moss;
For centuries it's helped folk cross.
A word once given, keep it true,
And trust will bridge the banks for you.
loiGiai: The moss-covered stone bridge has stood in the flowing water for hundreds of years, still joining the two banks. Words are like stones: once spoken, keep them firm. This verse is a reminder about keeping your word. Those who keep their promises are trusted, and that trust is the bridge between people, more lasting than anything showy.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: At home, if you promise your children or parents something, do your best to keep it. If you cannot, say so honestly and apologize.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Keep appointments and commitments with clients and colleagues. Promise only what you can deliver; that is a working person's greatest asset.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Keep your promise to yourself about a good habit, such as sleeping early or exercising. Lasting health grows from small commitments.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Once you have a study plan, keep it steady. Promise yourself and follow through, and your confidence in your abilities will grow.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts through faithfulness and words that match deeds. Don't make hasty promises; let your actions speak.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Repay loans on time and be transparent in partnerships. The trust you keep today opens many doors later.

loiKhuyen: Promise only what you can do, and do what you have promised. Trust is the strongest bridge.

tho: From mountain heights a clear spring flows,
Through rocks it murmurs as it goes;
Keep body gentle as that stream,
Eat well, sleep well, and strength will gleam.
loiGiai: A spring flows from the high mountain through rocky crevices, murmuring day and night and still running pure. This verse reminds you to care for body and mind as you would keep a stream clean: eat in moderation, sleep enough, move gently and keep your mind calm. Health doesn't arrive in a day, but caring for it a little each day gives you lasting strength.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A simple family meal with plenty of vegetables and less oil is a gift of health for everyone. Cook together and eat slowly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If you work for long hours, stand up to stretch and drink water. A healthy body is the foundation for good, lasting work.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Listen to your body. Eat regularly, sleep enough and drink enough water. If you take medication, follow your doctor's instructions and keep your follow-up appointments.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Enough sleep helps memory. Don't stay up too late studying; divide your time sensibly and take breaks between sessions.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A clear mind makes love gentle. Take walks with your partner, exercise together and look after each other.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Spending on health, like wholesome food and regular check-ups, is money well spent. Cut back on spending for unhealthy habits.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, go to bed thirty minutes earlier and drink one more glass of water. Guard your body as you would a spring.

tho: The little ferry waits ashore,
As faithful as it was before;
Good things may come a little late;
Live well and gently while you wait.
loiGiai: The little ferry still waits at the river landing, its heart not fading even when no passengers come. This verse speaks of faithful, calm waiting. Good things, a true friend or a fortunate meeting may come late, but they come to those who keep their hearts. While you wait, don't sit in sadness; live at ease and do your daily work well.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A relative may be far away, or the family may be hoping for something. Stay in touch and send your greetings, so those far away know there is always a landing waiting.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A job result or promotion may still be pending. Meanwhile, do your current work well and keep learning.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't let waiting make you neglect yourself. Eat proper meals, get outdoors and see friends to keep your heart at ease.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: The fruits of study take time to show. Keep working hard and don't compare your pace with others.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: The person you love may arrive when you least expect it. Keep a sincere heart, live joyfully and don't choose in haste out of impatience.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income can be thin at times, like an empty pier. Spend carefully, keep an emergency fund and be patient with honest work.

loiKhuyen: Waiting while still living joyfully is the most beautiful way to wait. Do today's work well.

tho: Halfway up, the breeze blows light;
Sit down and rest, regain your might.
The peak's still there, so have no fear;
Take one deep breath, then climb from here.
loiGiai: Halfway up the mountain, with a light breeze blowing, the wise climber sits down to rest within their strength. The summit is still there and isn't going anywhere. This verse reminds you that resting isn't giving up. The road is still long, so catch your breath, drink some water, look back at how far you have come, and then continue.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Set aside a weekend day for the whole family to relax, without talking about pressures. Resting together brings everyone closer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If work has worn you out, take a short leave or rearrange your workload. Working sustainably matters more than working fast.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body is signaling that it needs rest. Sleep enough, cut back on coffee and take gentle walks. If fatigue or pain lasts, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying without breaks leads to overload. Split your sessions and rest five to ten minutes after each part; your mind will absorb more.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love also needs moments of slowing down. Instead of demanding, rest together and talk gently.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't overwork yourself just to earn more. Health is your greatest capital; spend modestly so you don't have to strain.

loiKhuyen: Rest a little to go a long way. Today, give yourself some truly relaxed time.

tho: I bend to see the lake so wide;
My face shows clear, with clouds beside.
Blame others less; look first within,
And mend your faults: let peace begin.
loiGiai: Bending over the wide lake, you see your own reflection clearly among the clouds. This verse advises you to look at yourself: blame others less and examine yourself more. Everyone makes mistakes; what matters is noticing and correcting them. When you change first, the relationships around you gradually become more harmonious.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When there is disagreement at home, before blaming anyone, ask yourself what part you played. Admitting your share first eases the air.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Look back at how you work: what goes well and what needs fixing. Ask colleagues for feedback with an open mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Observe your daily habits for a week, including sleep times, meals and screen time, then choose one thing to adjust.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Review old tests and find the mistakes you make most often. Learning from your own errors is a fast and solid way to improve.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: In love, instead of asking the other person to change, see where you could be gentler and listen more.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Look back over last month's spending and find where money was wasted. Fixing small habits makes your finances steadier.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, take a few minutes to ask yourself: what did I do well today, and what should I improve?

tieuDe: The Little Basket Boat Learning to Row
tho: The little basket boat is small;
It knows the waves are wide and tall.
It practices near shore each day
Till steady hands can row away.
loiGiai: A small woven basket boat is among big waves. Its rower knows their own strength, so instead of rushing out to sea, they practice near the shore first. Little by little the hands grow used to the oar, and soon both near and far can be reached. This verse advises courage within your means: start with small tasks, gather experience, and then take on bigger ones.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Big household projects, such as repairs or moving, should be done in stages, with a budget planned ahead and advice from experienced people.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't take on too many tasks at once to prove yourself. Do the manageable part very well; your reputation will lead you to bigger work.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Increase exercise intensity gradually and warm up well. If you have an existing condition, ask your doctor before training hard.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Go from easy exercises to hard ones. Master the basics before advanced problems, and you will move faster in the long run.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Get to know a new relationship slowly. Begin with friendship, and trust will grow naturally.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: If you want to start a business, begin small with the capital you have and don't borrow beyond your means. Learn first, then expand.

loiKhuyen: Start small and practice until steady. Knowing your own strength is real courage.

tieuDe: The Bend in the Mountain Road
tho: The high pass bends and winds around;
The longer road is safe and sound.
In work and trade, don't rush or race;
Save coin by coin at steady pace.
loiGiai: The high mountain pass has many bends. Going around them seems slow, but those very bends keep travelers safe. This verse reminds you that the steadiest road isn't always the straightest. Earning and saving are the same: go steadily, spend thriftily, don't skip stages, and in time you will have enough.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Don't compare your family with others. Every family has its own path; build up little by little and live in harmony.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Promotion may not come as fast as you wish. See each bend as a chance to learn new skills, and never take shortcuts that break the rules.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: On mountain roads or long trips, rest well before you set out and don't drive when tired. With health, too, avoid looking for shortcuts.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Nothing replaces real practice. Follow a clear study plan rather than only learning tricks to get through exams.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love has its bends. Be patient and go through them together; don't let go just because the road isn't straight.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Lasting prosperity comes from hard work and thrift. Avoid gambling, high-interest loans and offers of unusually high returns. Slow and sure will bring enough.

loiKhuyen: A safe winding road is better than a risky shortcut. Set aside a small amount every month.

tieuDe: The Long River Reaches the Sea
tho: The long river finds the sea at last;
Its twists and turns are in the past.
So let old sorrows drift away;
Keep what was good, forgive today.
loiGiai: The long river passes through many twists and turns and finally reaches the open sea. What has passed, happy or sad, is part of that same flow. This verse advises letting go of old matters, keeping what was good and forgiving mistakes, both others' and your own. When your heart is as wide as the sea, old stumbles no longer weigh you down.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If old misunderstandings in the family still linger, take the first step to heal them. Forgiving isn't forgetting; it is giving each other a new beginning.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't carry the unpleasant memories of an old workplace into a new one. Keep the lessons and let the frustrations flow away.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Holding on to sorrow for a long time tires body and mind. Share with a trusted person, keep a journal and walk outdoors.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: One failure in your studies doesn't define you. Forgive yourself, learn from it and begin again with a lighter heart.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Let a past love flow out to sea. Keep the beautiful memories, give thanks, wish them peace, and open your heart to a new day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money spent unwisely can be a lesson for next time. Don't let regret lead you into emotional spending.

loiKhuyen: Today, forgive one old thing, perhaps something in yourself. Keep the good and let the sorrow drift away.

tieuDe: The Smooth Pebble in the Stream
tho: A pebble rests where waters flow;
Through years it rounds, so smooth and slow.
Let time's slow polish shape the soul;
With edges softened, we grow whole.
loiGiai: A pebble lies on the streambed, and as water flows over it through the years it becomes smooth and round. This verse speaks of self-cultivation: people too are polished by time, by friction and by learning. When we lose some of our sharp, hasty edges, we become kinder to one another. Don't shy away from challenges; they are making you better.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: At home, one harsh word less means a little more warmth. Practice speaking slowly and softly, especially with elders and young children.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Hard-to-hear feedback at work may be the water polishing the pebble. Listen, and keep what is right to improve yourself.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Frequent anger can affect your health. When upset, breathe deeply, sip some water and take a few steps before you speak.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Learning is a long polishing process. Be patient with difficult lessons and with your teachers' corrections.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when both people learn to soften. Let go of the ego a little, add gentle words, and friction will ease.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Building savings is like a pebble growing round: it takes time and patience. Keep spending discipline and don't follow the crowd.

loiKhuyen: Today, try replacing one harsh sentence with a gentle one. Soften, and your heart will be at peace.

tho: The rope bridge sways as breezes blow;
Look straight ahead, not down below.
Hold the rope firm and gently tread;
The far bank's joy is just ahead.
loiGiai: The rope bridge swings in the wind. If you look down you may hesitate, but if you look ahead and hold the rope firmly, every step is steady. This verse is for times when you are anxious before a challenge. Focus on the next step rather than the fear, trust your preparation, and joy will be waiting on the other side.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When the family faces something new, encourage each other to look ahead. A hand held at such a time is worth more than many words of advice.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Presentations, interviews or a new role may make you nervous. Prepare thoroughly, rehearse a few times, then step up with confidence.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Anxiety can make your heart race and disturb your sleep. Practice slow breathing and gentle exercise. If worry persists, don't hesitate to consult a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Before an exam, don't dwell on scores. Focus on each question, secure the ones you know and stay calm when you meet a hard one.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Opening up to someone you care about can feel daunting. Be sincere and gentle; whatever the outcome, you have been true to yourself.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Before a large expense, make a clear plan with a backup option. Good preparation means less worry.

loiKhuyen: Look ahead and hold firmly to the basics. One step at a time, you will cross the bridge.

tieuDe: The Rock Mountain in Wind and Rain
tho: Though rain may slant and winds may roar,
The mountain stands as it stood before;
Let praise and blame blow where they will,
Keep your heart steady, firm and still.
loiGiai: Rain slants and wind gusts from every direction, yet the rocky mountain stands still; clouds only linger on its peak and then drift away. Praise and criticism from outside are like the wind. This verse advises you to keep a steady heart and live by what you believe is right, without being swayed by what others say. Steady within, you can weather any hardship.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Every family has its own way of living. Don't let outside gossip cause hurt between you; trust and stand by one another.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Praise and criticism at work are normal. Take useful feedback, let groundless remarks pass and keep working with a calm mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A steady mind supports a healthy body. Keep regular routines and read less negative news. When stress builds up, find someone to talk to.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't let comparisons with friends discourage you. Pursue your goals at a pace that suits you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Trust your sincere feelings more than rumors. A steady relationship needs trust from both sides.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't chase spending or investment trends out of fear of falling behind. Stick to your own financial plan; steady is enough.

loiKhuyen: Listen to feedback, but hold firm to what you believe is right. A mountain doesn't move for the wind.

tho: For years away from pier and lane,
Now home, the bamboo stands again;
The old pier waits, as patient still,
With laughter, warmth, and old goodwill.
loiGiai: After many years away from the landing and the village, you return to find the bamboo row still standing, the old pier still waiting and familiar laughter sheltering the whole family. This verse carries a feeling of reunion and gratitude for your roots. However far you go, your old home and loved ones remain your support. Make time to return, visit and keep those bonds alive.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This is a good time to visit your hometown, your grandparents and parents. If you cannot go yet, a caring phone call is enough to make your family happy.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: You may meet old acquaintances or former colleagues again. Keep these relationships warm; sincere bonds often open doors.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: The air of home and a meal cooked by family help the spirit recover. Give yourself time to rest, and remind relatives to have health check-ups.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't forget the teachers and schools that taught you. A visit or a note of thanks also nourishes your love of learning.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love can come from what is familiar and close. Treasure the person who has always been by your side, even when you were far away.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Set aside part of your money to care for your family. Plan your spending so that trips home are always joyful and easy.

loiKhuyen: Call a loved one today, or set a date to visit. Your old home always has someone waiting.
